children: Apple Inc. (AAPL, Financials) faces a $2.7 billion (2 billion) lawsuit in Britain over its App Tracking Transparency guidelines.

The lawsuit was brought before London's Competition Appeal Tribunal on behalf of app developers who say Apple imposed more onerous limitations on tracking third parties than it did on its own services.
Apple added the feature in 2021 and has defended it as a key privacy precaution. The financial danger is beyond the damages claimed.

If regulators and courts compel Apple to modify its regulations, the company would lose a measure of control over how developers gather data and compete in its ecosystem. That pressure is mounting across Europe.
Germany recently forced Apple to alter its data-consent policies over worries about preferential treatment. Regulators in France, Italy and Poland have also looked at the framework.
The big question for investors is whether Apple's power to establish the rules for its App Store and advertising ecosystem is starting to be eroded by the ongoing regulatory problems.

The $2.7 billion judgment is a manageable figure for Apple given its size, but wider policy reforms could have a more lasting effect. The next spark will be Apple's formal answer and whether the UK tribunal authorizes the action to proceed to a full damages case.

title: Apple's App Rules Just Picked Up a $2.7 Billion Legal Risk
